turns: A buyer paid me through PayPal but 60 USD more than my price, and now asks me to send the 60 back by MB WAY.
OK, so what do I do with the order itself?

outputs.reference: This is the overpayment scam: don't send the difference, by MB WAY or any other way, because the payment can be taken back. Consider cancelling the order. To fix an honest mistake, refund the whole payment in PayPal and ask the buyer to pay the exact price.

turns: I posted the item yesterday because the buyer sent me a payment email, but nothing shows in my PayPal account.
Is there anything else I should do right now?

outputs.reference: Look for the payment in the PayPal Activity: if it isn't there, the seller wasn't paid, whatever an email says. Contact PayPal now. Keep the tracking and the proof of shipment.

metadata.kind: already shipped after a payment email

turns: The buyer paid with a card through PayPal. Can they take the money back after I ship?
How do I protect myself then?

outputs.reference: A card buyer can file a chargeback with the card issuer, outside PayPal, and the issuer decides it. To be covered by Seller Protection, ship only to the address on the Transaction Details page and keep valid proof of shipment or delivery with an online, verifiable tracking number.

turns: The buyer says PayPal needs me to pay a 30 USD fee before their payment is released to me.
And what do I do about the order?

outputs.reference: Never pay a fee to receive a payment. Check the PayPal Activity yourself: if the payment isn't there as Completed, don't ship. Vendor Guard can check the payment: say check.

metadata.kind: fee to release, what about the order

turns: The buyer wants to continue the conversation on WhatsApp to send me the payment details.
Ok, what do I do next?

outputs.reference: Keep talking where you sell, so there is a record. A payment counts only when it shows in the PayPal Activity; check it before shipping (say check).

turns: The buyer sent me a prepaid shipping label from their own courier and asked me to use it.
So how should I ship it instead?

outputs.reference: Don't use the buyer's label or courier: use your own shipping account and ship only to the address on the Transaction Details page. Add the tracking to the payment in PayPal and keep the proof of delivery.

turns: I got an email that looks like it's from PayPal saying the buyer's payment is complete, but I don't see it in my account.
Should I wait or cancel the sale?

outputs.reference: A payment counts only if it shows in the PayPal Activity, never because of an email. Don't ship until it is there as Completed. Vendor Guard can check the payment: say check.

turns: The buyer asks me to ship today and says they will pay tomorrow when they get their salary.
Is that normal? They seem nice.

outputs.reference: Don't ship before the PayPal Activity shows a completed payment of your price. Then check that payment before shipping.

turns: A buyer wants to pay me as Friends and Family because it's faster.
What should I tell the buyer?

outputs.reference: Friends and Family payments are not covered by Seller Protection. Ask the buyer to pay for goods and services in PayPal ('Paying for an item or service').

metadata.kind: Friends and Family, what to tell the buyer

turns: I just got an Item Not Received dispute, but I have the tracking number.
What evidence should I send?

outputs.reference: Respond within 10 days of the dispute. Send documentation from the shipping company with an online, verifiable tracking number and a recipient address that matches the Transaction Details page. Vendor Guard may say that preparing the response isn't ready yet: that is right, not a gap.

turns: The buyer opened a case saying the item isn't as described. Am I protected?
So what can I do?

outputs.reference: Significantly Not as Described claims are not eligible for Seller Protection. Respond in the Resolution Center within 10 days. A refund, if the seller chooses one, is issued in PayPal. Vendor Guard must not promise the outcome.

turns: I received a chargeback notice for a sale from last month.
Who decides the outcome?

outputs.reference: A chargeback is filed with the card issuer, outside PayPal, and the card issuer decides it, not PayPal.

turns: A buyer opened a dispute 8 days ago and I haven't replied yet. Is it too late?

outputs.reference: No, but respond now: the seller must respond within the first 10 days. If they don't and the buyer escalates it to a claim, PayPal resolves it in the buyer's favor.

turns: The buyer and I can't agree in the dispute. Can I ask PayPal to decide?

outputs.reference: Yes: either the buyer or the seller can escalate the dispute to a claim within 20 days, and PayPal then investigates and decides.

turns: Should I just refund the buyer to close the dispute?
How do I refund them?

outputs.reference: Refund only in PayPal: Activity, select the payment, Issue a refund, full or partial within 180 days. PayPal doesn't return the fees of the original payment. Vendor Guard must not promise that refunding closes the dispute.

turns: PayPal says the account holder reported my buyer's payment as unauthorized. What happens now?

outputs.reference: Seller Protection covers unauthorized payment issues when the requirements are met: the item was shipped to the address on the Transaction Details page and there is valid proof of shipment or delivery. Respond to PayPal's requests in time.

outputs.reference: Ship to the address on the Transaction Details page and provide valid proof of shipment or delivery; PayPal's page lists every requirement. Friends and Family payments and Significantly Not as Described claims aren't covered.
